title: High-Dose Insulin Euglycemia Therapy (HIET) — Dosing
keywords: regular insulin 1 unit per kg IV bolus then 0.5 to 1 unit per kg per hour infusion titrate to 10
dextrose 0.5 g per kg bolus if glucose under 250 then infusion
hypokalemia expected keep potassium 2.5 to 2.8 do not aggressively replace
onset 15 to 45 minutes inotropy not chronotropy monitor glucose
calcium channel blocker beta blocker poisoning cardiogenic shock
sources: Engebretsen KM, Kaczmarek KM, Morgan J, Holger JS. High-dose insulin therapy in beta-blocker and calcium channel-blocker poisoning. Clin Toxicol (Phila). 2011;49(4):277-283
St-Onge M, Anseeuw K, Cantrell FL, et al. Experts Consensus Recommendations for the Management of Calcium Channel Blocker Poisoning in Adults. Crit Care Med. 2017;45(3):e306-e315

changelog.change: Initial entry — weight-based HIET starting doses (regular insulin bolus + infusion range + titration ceiling, dextrose bolus and maintenance). Companion to tox-cardiac-meds; the HIET dosing-card follow-on named in that module's build note.

purpose: Weight-based starting doses for high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy — the workhorse for cardiogenic shock from calcium-channel-blocker or beta-blocker poisoning. Insulin here is an inotrope: it takes 15-45 min to work, so start it early and keep vasopressors and calcium running alongside. Titrate the infusion up (not the bolus) to effect, guided by cardiac output / perfusion, not a fixed number.

inputs.label: Current blood glucose (optional — for the dextrose decision)

formulas.label: Insulin infusion — alternative higher start (1 unit/kg/h)
Dextrose — bolus if glucose < 250 mg/dL (0.5 g/kg)
Dextrose maintenance — approx D10W rate (0.5 g/kg/h)

interpretation.label: Give the bolus of REGULAR insulin, then start the infusion immediately. Also give a dextrose bolus now unless the glucose is already > 250 mg/dL. Do not wait for a glucose result to start insulin in a crashing patient. Onset of inotropy is 15-45 min — continue calcium, vasopressors, and pacing in the meantime.

Standard start is 0.5-1 unit/kg/h. Titrate UP by 0.5-2 unit/kg/h every 10-30 min for inadequate perfusion / cardiac output — reported effective doses commonly reach 5-10 unit/kg/h; do not re-bolus to escalate. Wean once vasopressor requirement and perfusion improve; insulin often outlasts the pressors.

After the bolus, run a continuous dextrose infusion (D10W, or D25/D50 via central line for volume control) and check glucose every 15-30 min until stable, then hourly. Euglycemia target ~100-250 mg/dL; hypoglycemia can occur up to a day after insulin is stopped, so keep checking.

Potassium falls (intracellular shift, not total-body deficit). Keep serum K around 2.5-2.8 mEq/L and replace only to that floor — aggressive repletion causes rebound hyperkalemia when the insulin is weaned. Monitor K every 1-2 h. Watch for fluid overload from the dextrose volume; concentrate the dextrose and consider a diuretic.

notes: Use REGULAR insulin. HIET is first-line for moderate-to-severe CCB toxicity and a key adjunct for beta-blocker toxicity; it improves inotropy and metabolic substrate use without raising SVR, so it pairs with a vasopressor rather than replacing one. Central venous access is preferred for concentrated dextrose and potassium. Common pitfalls: starting too late, under-titrating the infusion, over-replacing potassium, and stopping dextrose monitoring too soon. Lipid emulsion, transvenous pacing, and VA-ECMO are the next tier for refractory shock. See tox-cardiac-meds for the full antidote decision.
buildNote: Formula engine — weight-based starting figures only; the titration ceiling (10 unit/kg/h) is shown as a computed number but escalation is clinical. Dextrose bolus is gated in prose on glucose < 250 (no conditional engine). D50 volume uses 0.5 g/kg = 1 mL/kg of D50W; D10 maintenance approximates 0.5 g/kg/h. Companion to tox-cardiac-meds and toxidromes-and-overdoses.
